fit: Review with re-presented sleep and perception studies
assessment: The review reuses the sleep comparison of 14 left-onset and 17 right-onset Parkinson participants with 17 chronically ill controls from PMID 18797256. The studies of spatial perception and sleep use different tests. In Figure 12 the review reverses the sleep-item scale for frequency display. Nocturnal hallucination ratings are not a separately counted visual-episode outcome for dried figs.

fit: Neuropathology review with tissue assay findings
assessment: The paper summarizes cortical Lewy body clinicopathology and describes work distinguishing presynaptic aggregates from conspicuous Lewy bodies. It reports mostly null correlations of broad body counts with clinical findings and cites regional temporal associations for formed visual hallucinations. Regional pathology, disease classification and episode frequency are distinct. No food intervention is described.

fit: Inherited neuroaxonal dystrophy case and tissue series
assessment: The study describes seven PLA2G6-associated cases with differing ages of onset. One adult case had transient visual hallucinations early in a progressive dystonia-parkinsonism syndrome and later had a cortical biopsy. The case description gives timing but no recurrence estimate. Its diagnosis, tissue findings and treatment history do not supply an idiopathic Parkinson food comparison.

The case series examines five families with complex early-onset parkinsonism and reuses previously reported clinical descriptions. Visual hallucinations appear in the background on earlier ATP13A2 follow-up. One FBXO7-family case developed psychosis during levodopa treatment, prompting clinicians to withdraw it. The authors give no visual episode count for this case or a dietary comparison.

RECOVER randomized 287 participants with Parkinson disease to the rotigotine patch or placebo. The distressing-hallucinations sleep item did not improve within the active group in the reported post hoc summary. A broader perception and hallucinations score and one serious visual-hallucination withdrawal are separate observations. The trial studied a patch and did not count visual episodes after dried-fig intake.

In five adults with a history of Dravet syndrome, motor slowness, hypomimia and perseveration resembled features seen in other disorders. One narrative describes recurring hallucinatory symptoms in adulthood and no indication of hallucinations during a later examination. The article does not classify those experiences by sensory modality or compare diagnosed Parkinson participants receiving dried figs.

The 14 left-onset and 17 right-onset Parkinson participants and 17 chronic-condition controls completed the Parkinson Disease Sleep Scale. Nocturnal hallucinations differed in the unadjusted comparison (overall p=.005). With mood adjustment, the left-onset group differed from controls (p=.007) and the right-onset group (p=.02). The measure represents reported nighttime frequency, without separate visual event counts or an assigned food exposure. The 2010 disconnection review reused this sample.

fit: Longitudinal Parkinson hallucination and sleep cohort
assessment: The authors followed 89 deliberately stratified Parkinson participants at five assessments. At six years 49 were interviewed and 40 were deceased or too ill to participate. Nightmares and vivid dreams were associated with concurrent hallucinations but did not predict subsequent hallucinations in initially unaffected participants in the abstract (OR 0.94, p=.51). The cohort does not test dried figs. The exact visual modality ascertainment and full outcome tables remain open.

The investigators compared 24 Parkinson participants who reported visual hallucinations with retained insight and 41 without prior visual hallucinations. The right fusiform signal was lower at a corrected cluster threshold. Higher right superior and middle temporal signals were described at an uncorrected threshold. These are group perfusion comparisons, without a dried-fig intervention or repeated visual episode counts.

The study used longitudinal clinical records and regional pathology in 63 cases with Lewy bodies, including 29 DLB cases, 18 Parkinson dementia cases and 16 with parkinsonism without dementia. Well-formed visual hallucinations were associated with Lewy body burden in the amygdala and parahippocampus. The visual phenotype and its timing differ from an event-frequency response to food.

fit: Postmortem plaque and Lewy body association
assessment: The authors compared 40 Parkinson autopsies with 20 age-matched controls. The cortical association was stronger in the subgroup with moderate or greater amyloid plaque burden. The [2011 Compta report] identifies 23 of its 56 Parkinson cases as partly assessed previously in this study. The abstract has no visual-episode recurrence or assigned dried-fig exposure.

fit: Exploratory analysis of the original RECOVER randomization
assessment: The paper reuses the RECOVER trial and describes post hoc subsets based on baseline symptom burden. The abstract gives sleep and quality-of-life items that favored rotigotine, mainly pain and mobility-related items. It supplies no separate hallucination-item estimate and notes the trial did not have statistical power for subgroup analyses. This is a reanalysis of the same randomization and not a dried-fig comparison.

fit: Original clinical observation later reused in a genetic series
assessment: The primary abstract describes a juvenile-onset parkinsonism case with motor phenomena and psychotic behavior. The later family series expressly reuses this case and its video, then reports an FBXO7 finding. Neither abstract reports a count of visual experiences. The exposure is not a dried-fig comparison, and the case is shared across the two publications.

The official results list one serious visual-hallucination event in one participant among 191 in the rotigotine safety group and zero among 96 in placebo. These denominators describe safety follow-up. The parent article's randomization was 190 versus 97. The comparison concerns a transdermal medication and reports no dried fig intake.

Eleven of 84 participants had 22 events recorded under a general hallucination term. The open-label extension drew from the RECOVER parent trial and has no parallel placebo group. Counts combine events within an individual and do not specify visual modality or a dried-fig contrast.
